## Scope note

The stated target `32` resolves to **PR #32** — `phase 4 close-out: lean plan tracker + docs/plans/`, merged 2026-07-24, **100% Markdown** (`CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, two `book/` pages, five `docs/plan*` files). It has no correctness surface and, being merged, nothing `--fix` could apply to the working tree. I confirmed that, then reviewed the real reviewable scope: the unmerged **slice 5.9 (exec-from-FS)** work on `feature/slice-5.9-exec-from-fs` — `git diff main...HEAD`, 23 files, +2519/−272 — plus the working-tree change to `.claude/settings.json` (an unrelated harness tool-matcher rename; no finding).

## Findings (4)

- **kernel/src/boot_image/elf.rs:133** — *medium*. `load_segment` now takes its page count from `PageBudget::charge`, which divides by `kernel_shared`'s `USER_PAGE_SIZE`, but strides the returned count by this crate's `mmu::PAGE_SIZE`. Before this diff the count was computed locally from `PAGE_SIZE`, so the two could not disagree. Concrete failure: a 16 KiB-granule port (plausible for Apple Silicon) changes `mmu::PAGE_SIZE` only — `charge` still returns `ceil(memsz/4096)`, and the loop maps that many 16 KiB pages, allocating 4× the frames and running four pages past the segment into the next one or into `SERVER_STACK_VA`. Silent; nothing asserts the equality.
- **servers/vfs/src/main.rs:1143** — *low*. `grant_test`'s doc states "There is no cycle: … PM never sends to VFS." Slice 5.9 makes PM a client of VFS (`VFS_EXEC_STAGE`), so the stated safety argument for the blocking prologue `ipc_send` is now false. The code is still safe (that send is confined to VFS's prologue), but the comment as written invites adding a VFS→PM send inside the receive loop, which would deadlock a PM blocked in `VFS_EXEC_STAGE` against a VFS blocked replying to it.
- **servers/vfs/src/main.rs:837** — *low*. `fs_lookup`'s summary line still says it returns `(inode, mode)`; this diff changed it to `(inode, mode, size)` and updated only the paragraph below.
- **kernel/src/boot_image/elf.rs:268** — *low (simplification)*. `match scan_brand_chunked(…) { Ok(_) => {} Err(e) => return Err(e) }` is a hand-rolled `?`.

## What I verified rather than assumed

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo clippy -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none --no-default-features -D warnings`, and the host test suites all pass; a full QEMU boot passes **all 85** `check-boot-log.sh` markers. I traced the grant path end to end (`verify_grant` arg order and `who_to`/seq/access checks, `ElfSource::read` bounds vs. `entry.len` and `user_range_ok`), the new frame-free paths in `load_segment` (no double free — `Frame` has no `Drop`), `read_whole`'s termination and `rw::advance` interaction, `path::parse`/`stage::parse_path` slicing, `EXEC_*` payload offsets against the 96-byte payload, MXBI pack order (`vfs` precedes `pm`, so PM's DS lookup resolves), VFS's 256 KiB `.bss` placement (RW `PT_LOAD` memsz `0x41000` at `0x105000`, ~700 KB clear of `SERVER_STACK_VA` at `0x200000`), and the `MAX_NOTE_BYTES` cap against the real SDK `hello` (`PT_NOTE` filesz `0x1c`, 8 phdrs — far inside the 256/64 caps). No bug found in any of those.

1. **elf.rs** — added `const _: () = assert!(PAGE_SIZE as u64 == USER_PAGE_SIZE);` with a comment explaining the coupling this slice introduced.
2. **elf.rs** — collapsed the brand-scan `match` to `scan_brand_chunked(source, &eh)?;`.
3. **vfs/main.rs** — rewrote the stale no-cycle comment to state the narrower invariant that actually holds (prologue-only send; nothing in the receive loop may send to PM).
4. **vfs/main.rs** — corrected the `fs_lookup` doc summary to `(inode, mode, size)`.

`ReportFindings` isn't available in this environment (I searched for it; only unrelated tools surfaced), so the findings are below in the required form.

## Review of PR #52 — exec-from-FS (slice 5.9)

I read every hunk of `git diff main...HEAD` plus the uncommitted working-tree changes, and traced the new paths end to end: `SYS_EXEC`'s grant form, `ElfSource`/`PageBudget`/`scan_note_segment`, `verify_grant`'s reuse, PM's `path::parse` → `vfs_exec_stage` → `sys_exec_grant`, VFS's `do_exec_stage`/`read_whole`/`stage.rs`, and init's `exec_denials`.

**The core of the slice holds up.** In particular I verified: `ElfSource::read` bounds every read against the declared length before either arm runs; `verify_grant` is called with `offset=0`/`CPF_READ` and its `who_to == caller` check makes a spoofed granter useless; the ELF is fully read before the point of no return, so every failure leaves the target on its old image (init's 8-probe battery really is the rollback proof); `load_segment` now frees a frame it allocated but could not fill or map; the grant-slot budget (2 permanent + 1 staged + 1 per-round out of 8) never exhausts; and `stage_len`/`VFS_EXEC_MAX`/`MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` are consistent with `build.rs`'s new size assert. Host tests (327) and kernel clippy (default and `--no-default-features`) are green, and `cargo fmt --all --check` passes after my edits.

### Findings

- `kernel/build.rs:203` — **medium**: the "load-bearing" DS publish-before-retrieve chain comment still reads `ds < tty < memory < mfs < vfs`, but slice 5.9 made PM a client of VFS via `vfs_endpoint()`'s `DS_RETRIEVE`. The array happens to satisfy `vfs < pm` (vfs at index 5, pm at index 8, with `sched`/`rs` between), so nothing breaks today — but the invariant the comment exists to protect is now undocumented, and moving `minixrs-pm` above `minixrs-vfs` would silently retire the `[diag pm] vfs.ds ok ep=` marker the same PR just made a required expectation. **Fixed**: chain updated to `ds < tty < memory < mfs < vfs < pm` with the `vfs.ds` lookup named.
- `kernel/src/arch/aarch64/userland.rs:511` — **low**: the `SERVER_STACK_VA` stack-page map folds *every* `MapError` into `ENOMEM`, which is exactly the stance this slice set out to end. Since exec-from-FS the ELF is an input, so an image whose own segments cover `0x0020_0000` now returns `MapError::AlreadyMapped` → `ENOMEM` ("the machine is out of frames") for what is really `ENOEXEC` ("this is not an image this kernel will run") — the same class of file `init`'s `not-elf` probe exists to distinguish. Cleanup and rollback were already correct; only the errno was wrong. **Fixed**: routed through the new `elf_errno(ElfError::Map(e))`, so only a genuine allocator failure stays `ENOMEM`.
- `userland/init/src/main.rs:562` — **low**: the `relative` probe's doc bullet opens with "`EINVAL`:" and then spends three lines correcting itself to `ENOENT` (which is what the code asserts). A reader skimming for the expected errno gets the wrong one. **Fixed**: bullet now leads with "**`ENOENT`, not `EINVAL`**".
- `tests/qemu-boot.expected:268` — **low**: the comment above the five C markers still says `hello` is "exec'd out of the boot archive", which this PR made false by dropping the module — and it sits directly under the new `src=grant` block that explains the opposite. Since these marker files are the repo's contract documentation, the contradiction is worth removing. **Fixed**: now says "exec'd out of the MinixFS root (slice 5.9 dropped the boot-archive copy)".
- `kernel/src/boot_image/elf.rs:132` — **low**, *not fixed*: `scan_brand_chunked` stages only the first `MAX_NOTE_BYTES` (256) of each `PT_NOTE`, while `kernel/build.rs`'s pack-time gate still calls the unbounded `brand::scan_brand`. The two can now disagree: a toolchain that emits more than 256 bytes of notes ahead of `.note.minixrs.ident` in the same segment passes the build and is refused at boot as unbranded, with only a `[brand] reject:` line to go on. Not reachable with this repo's `user.ld`/`hello.ld` rule (dedicated 28-byte `PT_NOTE`), but the SDK flavour has zero CI coverage and does not use `hello.ld`, so it is the one place the divergence could show up. I left it alone because narrowing `scan_brand` to match would weaken the host-side gate and widening `MAX_NOTE_BYTES` trades kernel stack for a case that cannot currently occur — but it deserves a line in the `MAX_NOTE_BYTES` doc comment recording that the pack-time check is *not* equivalent.

### Applied vs. skipped

Fixed in the working tree: the four items above marked **Fixed** (`kernel/build.rs`, `kernel/src/arch/aarch64/userland.rs`, `tests/qemu-boot.expected`, `userland/init/src/main.rs`). Re-verified afterwards with `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none --release` and the same with `--no-default-features` — all clean.

Skipped: the `MAX_NOTE_BYTES` divergence (any fix changes intended behaviour, see above). I also considered and deliberately dropped a report on grant-sequence pressure — `read_whole` now issues ~49 grants per `hello` exec, so `GRANT_MAX_SEQ` (2047) can wrap within a single 120 s boot, eroding `verify_grant`'s stale-id rejection — because no holder in the tree keeps a grant id across more than one round trip, so I could not construct a scenario where it actually misbehaves. It is inherent to the FS band's no-grant-offset rule rather than to this PR.

Note: `.claude/settings.json`, and the doc/`?`-cleanup hunks in `kernel/src/boot_image/elf.rs` and `servers/vfs/src/main.rs`, were already uncommitted before I started; the `PAGE_SIZE == USER_PAGE_SIZE` const assert in that working-tree `elf.rs` hunk is a good catch and closes the one real divergence I would otherwise have flagged (`PageBudget::charge` counting with `USER_PAGE_SIZE` while `load_segment` strides with `mmu::PAGE_SIZE`).</result>

Chain updated to `ds < tty < memory < mfs < vfs < pm`.
2. **`kernel/src/arch/aarch64/userland.rs:511` — low.** The `SERVER_STACK_VA` map folded *every* `MapError` into `ENOMEM` — the exact stance this slice set out to end. Since the ELF is now an input, an image whose segments cover `0x0020_0000` gives `AlreadyMapped` → `ENOMEM` ("out of frames") for what is really `ENOEXEC`, the class init's `not-elf` probe exists to distinguish. Cleanup/rollback were already right; only the errno was wrong. Routed through `elf_errno(ElfError::Map(e))`.
3. **`userland/init/src/main.rs:562` — low.** The `relative` probe's doc bullet opened with "`EINVAL`:" then spent three lines correcting itself to `ENOENT` (what the code asserts). Now leads with the right one.
4. **`tests/qemu-boot.expected:268` — low.** Comment above the five C markers still said `hello` is "exec'd out of the boot archive", which this PR made false by dropping the module — sitting directly under the new `src=grant` block saying the opposite.

A toolchain emitting >256 bytes of notes ahead of `.note.minixrs.ident` in one segment would pass the build and be refused at boot as unbranded, with only a `[brand] reject:` line. Unreachable with this repo's `user.ld`/`hello.ld` rule (dedicated 28-byte `PT_NOTE`) — but the SDK flavour has zero CI coverage and doesn't use `hello.ld`, so that's the one place it could surface. Narrowing `scan_brand` weakens the host gate; widening `MAX_NOTE_BYTES` spends kernel stack on a case that can't occur. Worth a line in the `MAX_NOTE_BYTES` doc comment recording that the pack-time check is *not* equivalent — say the word and I'll add it.

Also considered and dropped: grant-sequence pressure. `read_whole` issues ~49 grants per `hello` exec, so `GRANT_MAX_SEQ` (2047) can wrap within a 120 s boot, eroding `verify_grant`'s stale-id rejection. No holder in the tree keeps a grant id across more than one round trip, so no misbehaviour is constructible — and it's inherent to the FS band's no-grant-offset rule, not to this PR.
